title: Aluvihare Rock Temple

groundCutout.basis: Model-local outline of the mapped narrow cleft and photographed stone stair at its mouth. The independent surrounding relief remains intact.

terrainReference.basis: Original source terrain at the southeast mouth of the named rock cleft. Fine rock overhangs, the cleft grade and the historic approach are independently estimated.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap named shrine cleft and its four explicitly mapped outcrops. Cave’s 1896 photograph and contemporary written account identify the tiled veranda and approach within the cleft.
mapIdentity.scope: Named OSM way 1197751507 outlines the narrow northwest-southeast temple cleft, between four specifically mapped bare-rock outcrops. Shared vertices and the Southeast entry from the road fix the approach and constrain the left veranda and inner stair.

note: Cave’s eyewitness account places the tiled veranda on the left of the approach, with a cavern behind it. His photograph fixes the basic masonry, stair sequence and overhanging rock; component sizes, hidden backs and the alignment within the modern map are estimated.
